summary.plain: A tank of nearly six tonnes of liquid xenon, watched by light sensors, that records the tiny flash made if a dark matter particle -- or a neutrino -- bumps into a xenon atom. It is the enlarged, cleaner successor to the XENON1T detector, in the same underground hall in Italy.
summary.technical: Dual-phase (two-phase) xenon TPC, 8.5 t total / 5.9 t active liquid xenon, in LNGS Hall B. Upgrade of the XENON1T detector, reusing its water shield; adds a cryogenic radon-distillation column and a dedicated neutron veto.
